advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the finally-block key-revert succeeded (or delete by whichever key currently exists) so a failed revert cannot silently leak the project and break fixture teardown.
evidence: test_transport.py:581-585 `_admin_request(f"/rest/api/2/project/{new_project_key}", method="PUT", payload={"key": jira_dc_project})` — return value ignored

conftest.py:427-428 `status, body = _request(f"/rest/api/2/project/{key}", method="DELETE") ... assert status in (204, 200), f"deleting scratch project {key} failed..."` — teardown deletes by the ORIGINAL key
Comment at test_transport.py:579-580 asserts the revert is what stops a project leak, but nothing checks the revert actually succeeded
advisory.finding: The finally-block project-key revert is best-effort (its HTTP status is discarded), so a failed revert leaves the project under `new_project_key`; the `jira_dc_project` fixture then deletes by the ORIGINAL key, gets a 404, trips its own `assert status in (204, 200)`, and leaks the project — the exact outcome the finally comment claims to prevent.
scenarios: DC transiently refuses the rename-back, or the new key collides so the PUT 500s/400s
advisory.suggested_fix: In the finally block, capture the revert status and assert it is 200; alternatively have teardown tolerate deletion by either key. Fail loudly if the project cannot be restored to its original key.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Register the created issue with `track_issue` so it is explicitly deleted and confirmed gone independent of the project cascade.
evidence: test_transport.py:539 `created = dc_transport.create_issue(...)` with no subsequent `track_issue(...)` call
test_transport.py:467 the deletion sibling deletes the issue explicitly
conftest.py:343-351 track_issue teardown asserts the DELETE status then polls the direct endpoint to 404 — skipped for an untracked issue
advisory.finding: The issue created by this test is never registered with `track_issue`, unlike every sibling live test; its cleanup depends entirely on the project-delete cascade, so if the project teardown fails (e.g. after a failed key-revert) the issue also leaks and its direct-endpoint 404 is never confirmed.
scenarios: Any run where the project teardown does not complete

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive a guaranteed-unique, non-colliding new project key (e.g. a fresh random suffix that is verified not to already exist) instead of a deterministic single-char mutation.
evidence: conftest.py:156-159 keys are `RBJ` + 4 random ascii_uppercase, so the derived key keeps the RBJ prefix and 3 shared random chars
advisory.finding: `new_project_key` is derived by truncating the last char of the scratch key and appending 'Z', keeping the shared `RBJ` prefix and leaving only 3 random chars distinguishing it; when the original random suffix already ends in 'Z' the pre-rename `assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project` errors the test, and there is a non-trivial collision chance with a concurrently existing scratch project.
scenarios: A scratch key whose 4th letter is 'Z' (1/26 of runs) fails at line 544; parallel runs risk key collision on the rename PUT

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'recorded not asserted' docstring with the status allowlist assertion — either drop the assertion or narrow the docstring claim to 'the id resolution is asserted; the stale-key status is only sanity-bounded'.
evidence: test_transport.py:532-533 `The reading is recorded rather than asserted, so this test reports the answer instead of encoding a guess as a contract.`
test_transport.py:566-568 `assert stale_status in (200, 301, 302, 404), (f"unexpected stale-key status {stale_status}; record it and widen this list")`
dropped.finding: The docstring states the stale-key reading is 'recorded rather than asserted', but the test asserts `stale_status in (200, 301, 302, 404)`; a genuinely novel status (e.g. 500 or a redirect code outside the list) fails the folklore cell instead of merely recording it — coupling the 'settle the folklore' evidence to a hardcoded status allowlist.
scenarios: DC returns a status outside the allowlist for a stale key

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the _best_effort collapse of set_last_get/clear_absent wrappers in outbound_differ.py is in scope for 7c26, or split it into its own module-size/refactor ticket.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:169-176: "One helper for the three bookkeeping calls this module makes (``set_last_get`` / ``note_absent_or_rekey`` / ``clear_absent``) ... Collapsed under bug 7c26 rather than for tidiness: this module sits at the LOCKED module-size cap, so wiring the move-aware absence path had to buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments."

Ticket 7c26 Approach: 'This is deliberately ADDITIVE rather than a re-keying of the store' — only the note_absent_or_rekey wiring is authorized; set_last_get/clear_absent are unrelated absence-bookkeeping paths the ticket does not touch.
dropped.finding: outbound_differ._best_effort collapses the pre-existing per-member bookkeeping wrappers (set_last_get / clear_absent, which are unrelated to the move/re-key behavior) into one generic helper — an opportunistic refactor of unrelated wiring, done to reclaim module-size-cap headroom rather than implementing anything 7c26 promises.
dropped.suggested_fix: If only the note_absent_or_rekey call site needs wiring under 7c26, keep the existing per-member wrappers for set_last_get/clear_absent and add just the one new guarded call; land the three-into-one _best_effort collapse as a separate refactor/size-cap ticket.
